question: Should `policy watch --interval-ms` continue accepting numerically equivalent plus-prefixed and zero-padded decimal spellings, or should Policy adopt canonical-decimal-only syntax as a deliberate breaking contract?
rationale: The current parser explicitly accepts these aliases, the public documentation does not prohibit them, and the examples resolve to the same interval; rejecting them is therefore a product compatibility choice rather than a demonstrated bug fix.

options.title: Preserve equivalent spellings
options.body: Remove the canonical-string equality gate and its rejection test while retaining existing range and malformed-number validation.

options.title: Adopt canonical-only syntax
options.body: Obtain explicit Policy-owner approval, document the stricter CLI contract, and provide real before/after/control CLI proof before merge.

options.title: Pause this tightening
options.body: Close or defer the PR if canonical spelling has no demonstrated operator benefit worth the compatibility cost.

recommendation.title: Preserve equivalent spellings
recommendation.body: Remove the canonical-string equality gate and its rejection test while retaining existing range and malformed-number validation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest area-specific routing candidate identified in the review timeline for the Policy CLI contract.
